usdRate.sourceName: European Central Bank euro reference rate (USD)
usdRate.note: EUR 1 = USD 1.1172, so about EUR 0.895 per US dollar; World Bank 2025 average 0.885.

inflation_cpi.sourceName: Trading Economics (Statistik Austria CPI, September 2026 final)
inflation_cpi.note: CPI 3.6% year on year in September 2026 (3.2% in August), final figure published 16 October 2026; secondary source because statistik.at was not read directly. World Bank 2025 average 3.5%.

inflation_projection.sourceName: ECB 2% medium-term target; Austrian CPI 3.6% (Sep 2026), 3.5% in 2025 (World Bank)
inflation_projection.note: The ECB 2% target is credible over the long run but Austrian inflation has run well above the euro-area average for several years, so 2.5% is used for planning.

policy_rate.sourceName: European Central Bank, key ECB interest rates (deposit facility)
policy_rate.note: Austria uses the euro; ECB deposit facility rate 2.50% (main refinancing 2.65%) since 16 September 2026, held on 29 October 2026.

savings_account_rate.sourceName: ECB MFI interest rate statistics: Austrian banks, overnight deposits from households (new business)
savings_account_rate.note: Average rate on household overnight deposits in Austria, August 2026; notice deposits up to 3 months (typical online savings accounts) paid 1.94%.

fdr_3m_rate.note: ECB/OeNB MFI statistics only publish deposits with agreed maturity up to 1 year as one bucket (2.15% in August 2026); no 3-month term deposit rate found; OeNB tables and comparison sites were not reachable.

fdr_1y_rate.sourceName: ECB MFI interest rate statistics: Austrian banks, household deposits with agreed maturity up to 1 year (new business)
fdr_1y_rate.note: Bucket covers all fixed terms up to one year; 1-2 years paid 2.18% and over 2 years 2.05% in August 2026.

dps_rate.note: Austria's monthly-deposit savings contract is the Bausparvertrag (building-society savings with a state premium); no current average rate was found from an official source.

bank_deposit_avg_rate.sourceName: ECB MFI interest rate statistics: Austrian banks, household deposits with agreed maturity (outstanding amounts)
bank_deposit_avg_rate.note: Average rate on all outstanding household term deposits; household overnight deposits paid 0.45%. World Bank FR.INR.DPST has no Austria figure.

sanchayapatra_5y_rate.note: Bundesschatz (retail federal savings product sold online by the Austrian Treasury, terms 1 month to 10 years) exists, but bundesschatz.at loads its rates by script and no figure could be read.

tbill_91d_rate.note: Austrian Treasury Bills are auctioned by OeBFA (latest auction 27 October 2026) but the result pages read did not show yields.

tbond_5y_rate.note: No 5-year Austrian government bond yield found: Trading Economics and worldgovernmentbonds.com pages read showed no 5-year figure and OeNB publishes only a weighted average (3.59% at 13.98 years residual maturity, 23 Oct 2026).

tbond_10y_rate.sourceName: Trading Economics, Austria 10-year government bond yield
tbond_10y_rate.note: ECB long-term (10-year) convergence yield for Austria was 3.69% in September 2026.

tax_bank_interest.sourceName: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, Austria income determination
tax_bank_interest.note: Final withholding tax (KESt) of 25% on bank deposit interest; 27.5% on publicly placed bonds.

tax_sanchayapatra_profit.sourceName: Bundesschatz (Austrian Treasury) FAQ; PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries
tax_sanchayapatra_profit.note: 27.5% KESt is withheld automatically on Bundesschatz interest for Austrian residents.

deposit_insurance_limit.note: EUR 100,000 per depositor per bank; up to EUR 500,000 in special cases set out in the scheme rules.

credit_card_rate_cap.note: No legal cap; the ECB/OeNB series for extended credit card credit to Austrian households is empty and no typical card rate source was reachable (revolving loans and overdrafts averaged 5.92% in August 2026).

equity_return_low.sourceName: ATX 6,420 on 30 Oct 2026, up 33.5% in a year; after-tax 1-year deposit 1.6%
equity_return_low.note: Low case: Austrian shares deliver little more than safe deposits over a long period, as in the 2007-2016 decade.

equity_return_base.sourceName: ATX price index (Trading Economics); 1-year deposit 2.15% less 25% KESt = 1.6%
equity_return_base.note: The ATX has done well over 10 years, but the base is capped at the after-tax safe rate plus about 4 points because the index is small and bank- and energy-heavy.

equity_return_high.sourceName: ATX price index (Trading Economics); global equity long-run returns
equity_return_high.note: High case: a diversified euro equity fund matching long-run global equity returns of about 7-8% in euros.

gold_return_low.sourceName: Gold USD 3,876/oz on 30 Oct 2026, 31% below the January 2026 high
gold_return_low.note: Low case: gold barely keeps up after the 2025-26 spike, with no help from the euro.

gold_return_base.sourceName: Gold price history (Trading Economics); ECB 2% inflation target
gold_return_base.note: Base case: dollar gold rises roughly with world inflation plus a little, and the euro is assumed stable against the dollar over the long run.

gold_return_high.note: High case: a repeat of gold's strong 2005-2025 trend in euro terms.

fixed_income_return_low.sourceName: Household notice deposits 1.94% less 25% KESt (ECB MFI statistics)
fixed_income_return_low.note: Low case: easy-access savings after tax, with rates drifting lower.

fixed_income_return_base.sourceName: Household deposits up to 1 year 2.15% less 25% KESt = 1.6%
fixed_income_return_base.note: Base case: after-tax 1-year term deposit rate.

fixed_income_return_high.note: High case: holding long government bonds or long Bundesschatz terms after tax.

life_claim_settlement_rate.note: The FMA and the Austrian insurance association do not publish an industry life claim settlement ratio that could be found; fma.gv.at refused automated access.

insurance_term_premium_table.note: Term life (Risikolebensversicherung) is widely sold, but comparison sites refused automated access and no published premium table was found.

health_hospitalisation_cost.note: Public hospital care is covered by statutory health insurance with a small daily patient contribution; no official figure for a typical out-of-pocket cost of a major private or mid-range hospital stay was found.

health_premium_table.note: Private supplementary hospital insurance (Sonderklasse) is sold, but no published premium table per EUR 100,000 of cover was found; premiums are not quoted per sum insured.

goal_inflation_health.sourceName: Eurostat/ECB HICP Austria, health: 5.3% year on year in December 2025
goal_inflation_health.note: Health prices have run above headline inflation; 4% is used as a long-run planning figure.

goal_inflation_education.sourceName: Eurostat/ECB HICP Austria, education: 5.2% year on year in December 2025
goal_inflation_education.note: Education prices (mainly private schooling and courses; public education is free) have risen faster than headline inflation; 4% is used for planning.

life_expectancy.sourceName: UN World Population Prospects via georank.org
life_expectancy.note: Men 80.2, women 84.7 (UN WPP estimate for 2026); World Bank 2024 figure 82.0.

life_table_remaining.sourceName: UN World Population Prospects via georank.org
life_table_remaining.note: Remaining years computed from georank's expected age at death by current age (UN WPP 2026 estimate).

support_ratio.sourceName: World Bank SP.POP.DPND.OL (2025); UN WPP 2024 via populationpyramid.net (2040, 2065)
support_ratio.note: 100 / old-age dependency ratio: 32.6 (2025, World Bank), 48.3 (2040) and 58.9 (2065, populationpyramid.net/austria/2065/).

retirement_age_default.note: Regular pension age 65; women's age rises by half a year every 6 months from 2024 (61-61.5 in 2026) and reaches 65 for women born from 1 July 1968. Minimum 15 insurance years.

retirement_age_government.note: Federal civil servants retire under the Civil Service Act (BDG 1979 s.13); the RIS legal database blocked automated access and no other source read stated the age.

retirement_return_low.note: Low case: easy-access savings after tax.

retirement_return_base.sourceName: Household deposits up to 1 year 2.15% less 25% KESt = 1.6%
retirement_return_base.note: Base case capped at the after-tax 1-year term deposit rate.

retirement_return_high.note: High case: a ladder of longer government bonds and Bundesschatz terms after tax, slightly below the 10-year yield.

retirement_accumulation_return_low.note: Low case for a balanced mix if shares lag.

retirement_accumulation_return_base.note: Base case: roughly half shares at 5.5% and half safe fixed income at about 1.6-2.6% after tax.

retirement_accumulation_return_high.note: High case for a growth-leaning balanced mix.

old_age_allowance_monthly.note: Not a separate social pension: a means-tested top-up that raises a pension to EUR 1,308.39 a month (single person, 2026); requires legal residence. Rates rise 3.3% in 2027.

old_age_allowance_eligibility.note: Paid only to people who draw a pension and whose total income is below the reference rate; ages shown are the regular pension ages (women's age rising to 65 by 2033).

gratuity_rule.sourceName: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, Austria other taxes (employee provision fund 1.53%)
gratuity_rule.note: Severance pay (Abfertigung neu): employers pay 1.53% of gross pay, including the 13th and 14th salaries, into an employee provision fund; 1.53% x 14 monthly salaries = about 6.4 days of pay per year of service, plus fund returns.

public_pension_scheme.note: Compulsory statutory pension insurance (employee 10.25%, employer 12.55% of gross pay); pensions are adjusted yearly by consumer-price inflation from August to July (2.95% for 2027 up to EUR 6,930 a month) and taxed as income.

fdr_3m.note: Also sold as a term savings book (Kapitalsparbuch).

dps.note: Regular monthly saving over 6 years with a small state premium; offered by building societies.

sanchayapatra_5y.localNameEn: Federal savings product of the Republic of Austria
sanchayapatra_5y.note: Sold online directly by the Austrian Treasury to individuals, fixed terms from 1 month to 10 years; 27.5% KESt withheld.

tbill_91d.note: Auctioned by the Austrian Treasury mainly to institutions.

equity_fund.note: Retail mutual and index funds are widely available; gains taxed at 27.5%.

gold.note: No restriction on buying physical gold.

centralBank.name: Oesterreichische Nationalbank
centralBank.note: Part of the Eurosystem; monetary policy set by the European Central Bank.

insuranceComplaints.name: Finanzmarktaufsicht (FMA), consumer information and complaints
insuranceComplaints.note: The FMA takes complaints about supervised insurers; disputes go to the civil courts.
